question: A team is implementing termination logic for an autonomous refactoring agent. Loop A exits when response.stop_reason == "end_turn". Loop B exits when the assistant's final text block is non-empty, on the assumption that any explanatory text means Claude is finished. Which loop correctly implements the standard termination pattern?
options: A) Loop A, because stop_reason directly reports whether Claude finished its turn without requesting a tool, which is the documented signal
B) Loop B, because a populated final text block is treated as the only reliable indicator that Claude has stopped requesting further tool calls
C) Neither loop works, because the API only signals completion through the total count of content blocks returned in the response
D) Both loops behave identically in practice, since stop_reason and trailing text emptiness always change together on every response
correct_answers: A) Loop A, because stop_reason directly reports whether Claude finished its turn without requesting a tool, which is the documented signal
explanations: Correct. Claude can emit explanatory text alongside a tool_use block in the same turn, so checking for text presence stops the loop too early; stop_reason is the structured, authoritative field.
Incorrect. A response can include commentary text while still requesting another tool, so non-empty text does not reliably mean the turn is finished.
Incorrect. Content block counts vary with output style and are not a documented completion signal in the Messages API.
Incorrect. Text presence and stop_reason are not guaranteed to move together; a turn can carry both a tool_use block and accompanying text.
